subject: Recap: Migration compatibility & hyperscaler comparison \u0014 next tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
To: Michael Tan <michael.tan@finco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Migration/compatibility eval & next tests (FinCo)

Hi Michael / Sara \u0014

Great to meet you both on the call today. Quick recap and agreed next steps so we can keep momentum on the migration + hyperscaler comparison: 

1) Goals we heard
- Replace OpenAI endpoints with minimal app changes
- Match or improve latency & cost per token vs current hyperscaler usage
- Validate prompt parity and output quality for core customer flows (KYC summarization, anonymization, credit policy Q&A)

2) Agreed technical tests (we'll help run/score these)
- SDK swap: replace base URL + API key, run smoke tests against 50 representative prompts (see attached prompt-diff-template.csv)
- Prompt-diff: run side-by-side comparisons vs OpenAI and one hyperscaler model (Bedrock/Vertex) for the 50 prompts; capture automated diff metrics + manual spot checks
- Performance benchmark: latency/throughput at target concurrency (5-20 qps) and token-length distribution like your production traces
- Security/compliance: confirm KMS support and audit-log retention for Dedicated/Private if required

3) Owners & timing
- Redwood: provide migration checklist, sample OpenAI-compatible snippets, and the prompt-diff template by EOD today (attachments). Aditya will own the test plan and run an initial pass with your test keys.
- FinCo: run the SDK-swap smoke tests and surface any prompt/parity failures by next Tue (2026-03-17).

4) Hyperscaler comparison notes (high level)
- Hyperscalers can be attractive for integrated infra but often trade off higher per-token cost and limited runtime optimizations for inference (we'll show numbers once we run the benchmark).
- Redwood differentiators we highlighted: OpenAI-compatible API (minimal app change), smart routing/fallbacks, KV/prefix caching to reduce cost, and per-route observability for regressions.

Attachments: migration-checklist.pdf, prompt-diff-template.csv, redwood-openai-compat-snippet.txt

If that matches your notes, we'll schedule a 30-min check-in next Wed to go through results.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.example.com | +1 415-555-0199

Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Migration/compatibility eval & next tests (FinCo)

Thanks Marissa \u0014 this looks good and aligned. A couple quick clarifications before we start running tests: 

1) When you say "OpenAI-compatible API", do you mean the same endpoints (completions/chat/embeddings) and same request/response shapes so our existing SDK calls don't need prompt engineering changes?
2) For the hyperscaler comparison, which model variants will you run against by default? We currently use gpt-4o on OpenAI and a mix of LLMs on Bedrock for embeddings.
3) Security: does Redwood support customer-managed KMS keys for encryption-at-rest, and will we be able to see a full audit trail for admin operations?

We'll start the smoke SDK swap next week. Can Aditya be looped in for the test keys?

-Michael
Michael Tan
Head of AI Engineering | FinCo
Michael.Tan@finco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
To: Michael Tan <michael.tan@finco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Migration/compatibility eval & next tests (FinCo)

Great questions \u0014 answers inline: 

> 1) Same endpoints / shapes?
Yes. Redwood exposes an OpenAI-compatible surface for completions, chat, and embeddings (request/response JSON shapes are compatible). Typical SDK swap is changing the base URL and apiKey variable; we included a small snippet in the attached "redwood-openai-compat-snippet.txt". There are a couple of edge cases to watch for (streaming token metadata and custom response fields) \u0014 we'll annotate those in the snippet. In practice most customers see zero changes to prompt text.

> 2) Which hyperscaler models?
We'll run the side-by-side against your current config: gpt-4o (OpenAI), and for hyperscaler we'll test one representative LLM from Bedrock and one from Vertex (we'll select nearest-analog variants with similar instruction-tuning). If you have a preferred Bedrock model name, share it and we'll include it.

> 3) KMS & audit trail?
Yes \u0014 customer-managed keys are supported on Redwood Private and Dedicated deployments via our KMS/HSM integrations, and we provide audit logs for admin operations (login, key changes, rollouts). For hosted plans we can discuss contractual SSO/KMS options (we'll surface specifics if you need them for procurement).

Next steps: Aditya, can you share the technical test plan + minimal code examples and confirm which metrics you'll collect (latency p50/p95, cost per token, semantic-diff score, and a small manual quality checklist)?

Michael/Sara, once you share a test key we'll kick off the initial SDK-swap smoke tests and return a results pack.

Thanks,
Marissa

---
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example.com>
To: Michael Tan <michael.tan@finco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Recap: Migration/compatibility eval & next tests (FinCo)

Hi Michael \u0014 quick technical plan and minimal swap examples. I'll run the initial pass once you share the test keys.

Test plan (initial pass)
- Smoke (15-50 prompts): verify request/response shapes, streaming parity, and token accounting.
- Prompt-diff (50 prompts): run against OpenAI (gpt-4o), Redwood default, Bedrock analog; capture tokens consumed, p50/p95 latency, semantic-diff (BLEU/ROUGE-lite + custom embeddings-distance), and a manual quality pass for 10 edge prompts.
- Load: replay a 10-minute window at 10 qps with average prompt length 120 tokens to measure throughput and tail latencies.

Metrics we will collect
- p50/p95 latency (ms) and throughput (req/s)
- tokens_in/tokens_out and cost estimate per 1M tokens
- semantic-diff score per prompt and overall distribution
- number of prompts with "meaningful divergence" flagged for manual review

Minimal code swap (OpenAI-compatible)
- cURL example:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDWOOD_KEY>" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-1.3", "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the following..."}]}'

- Node (openai-style) example (change base URL only):
  const OpenAI = require('openai');
  const client = new OpenAI({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, baseURL: 'https://api.redwood.example.com/v1' });
  const res = await client.chat.completions.create({ model: 'redwood-1.3', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: '...' }] });

Edge notes:
- Streaming: we support chunked SSE streams; meta fields are present but we may surface them under slightly different keys \u0014 we will provide a mapping table in the snippet file.
- Embeddings: payload shapes are compatible; we recommend a small normalization step for cosine thresholds when comparing across model families.

Attachments: prompt-diff-template.csv (attached)

I'll run the smoke pass as soon as you drop a short-lived test key (or we can use our sandbox keys if you prefer to run the client-side tests).

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.example.com
